analyzed_vuln.description: Double-free of flag arrays due to ownership confusion between dictionary entries and alias table entries. `parse_aliasf()` stores pointers returned by `decode_flags()` into `aliasf`. Later, when dictionary words use alias flags (`get_aliasf`), their `hentry->astr` points directly to those same `aliasf` buffers. During teardown, `HashMgr::free_table()` calls `free_flag(ptr->astr, ptr->alen)`, and `free_flag` may delete `astr` even when it is alias-owned (it only skips free when `aliasf` is non-empty and `ONLYUPCASEFLAG` is not set). Then `HashMgr::~HashMgr()` unconditionally iterates `aliasf` and `delete[]`s each entry again, causing the ASan double-free seen at destructor line 133.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: PoV must define an AF alias table (`parse_aliasf`) and then create at least one dictionary entry that references an alias index so `hentry->astr` aliases `aliasf[index-1]`. With crafted numeric flags in FLAG num mode (as in the PoV), cleanup path is reached: `Hunspell` destruction -> `HashMgr::free_table` frees the aliased flag buffer once, then `HashMgr::~HashMgr` frees `aliasf` buffers a second time. Trigger does not require large input; malformed/edge AF entries that still allocate alias buffers are sufficient.
